items.exampleEn: The bad-tempered driver kept shouting at other cars.
items.exampleZh: 那個脾氣暴躁的駕駛一直對其他車子大吼。

items.exampleEn: Many students are fed up with having tests every week.
items.exampleZh: 許多學生受夠了每週都要考試。

items.exampleEn: I didn't have the guts to jump into the cold lake.
items.exampleZh: 我沒有膽量跳進冰冷的湖裡。

items.exampleEn: She answered impolitely and walked away.
items.exampleZh: 她很沒禮貌地回了一句就走開了。

items.exampleEn: A cup of warm tea helped calm my nerves.
items.exampleZh: 一杯溫茶幫我平復了緊張的情緒。

items.exampleEn: Losing the match hurt his self-confidence for a while.
items.exampleZh: 輸掉比賽讓他的自信心受挫了一陣子。

items.exampleEn: She became more self-confident after she started her own business.
items.exampleZh: 她開始自己創業之後，變得更有自信了。

items.sentenceEn: I'm fed up with waiting; let's order without him.
items.sentenceZh: 我等煩了，我們不等他先點餐吧。

items.audioEn: My neighbor's dog is bad-tempered, so I always cross the street when I see it.
items.audioZh: 鄰居的狗脾氣很壞，所以我一看到牠就會過馬路避開。
items.questionZh: 說話者看到那隻狗時會怎麼做？

items.sentenceEn: He impolitely interrupted the speaker to ask about lunch.
items.sentenceZh: 他很沒禮貌地打斷講者，問午餐的事。

items.sentenceEn: Joining the drama club gave her more self-confidence.
items.sentenceZh: 加入戲劇社讓她更有自信心。

items.stemEn: After months of practice, she felt ____ enough to sing in front of the whole school.
items.stemZh: 練習了好幾個月後，她覺得夠有自信，可以在全校面前唱歌了。

items.stemEn: It takes real ____ to tell your boss that he is wrong.
items.stemZh: 要告訴老闆他錯了，需要真正的膽量。

items.passageEn: Last month, I gave my first presentation at work. The night before, my nerves were so bad that I couldn't sleep. My manager, a self-confident woman who is an experienced presenter, told me to practice in front of a mirror. During the talk, a man in the back row impolitely walked out in the middle, but I kept going. It took guts, but I finished, and afterward I could feel my self-confidence growing.
items.passageZh: 上個月，我在公司做了第一次簡報。前一晚我緊張到睡不著。我的經理是一位很有自信、經驗豐富的簡報者，她要我對著鏡子練習。簡報中，後排有個男人很沒禮貌地中途離場，但我繼續講下去。這需要膽量，但我講完了，之後我感覺到自己的自信心在增長。

referenceEn: My nerves are always bad before a competition.
I always suffer from nerves before a race.
rubricZh: 要用 nerves（例如 my nerves are bad、suffer from nerves 等）
「比賽」可寫，例如 a competition、a race、a game 等
頻率副詞位置正確即可（例如放在一般動詞前 always suffer、be 動詞後 are always 等）

items.instructionZh: 用 bad-tempered 造一個句子，描述你自己或身邊一個脾氣不好的人或動物。
referenceEn: I become bad-tempered when I'm hungry.
Our old cat is bad-tempered and hates being picked up.
rubricZh: 句子要用到 bad-tempered（例如 become bad-tempered、is bad-tempered）
時態配合內容（例如 become、is 等）

resolvedAfterFinalReview.message: 第②關 issue 結案：評分要點寫死位置：「always 放在一般動詞前」——若學生寫 "Before a competition, I am always a bag of nerves" 或 "My nerves are always bad before a game"，always 在 be 動詞後也正確，會被誤判。建議「頻率副詞位置正確（例如一般動詞前、be 動詞後）」。
resolvedAfterFinalReview.resolution: 已修正：見本檔 resolvedAfterFinalReview 中 items/14 的修正紀錄。

resolvedAfterFinalReview.message: 第②關 issue 結案：疑似不自然："I always have nerves before a competition" 較少見，常見為 "suffer from nerves"、"My nerves are always bad before…"。建議 ref1 改成 "My nerves are always bad before a competition." 之類。
